subject: Dedicated capacity validation: latency / concurrency / streaming clarification
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@helixai.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity validation: latency / concurrency / streaming clarification

Hi Alex —

Great to meet you and the HelixAI team earlier. Quick recap of the performance-related asks that came up during the demo and the proposed next steps so we can align on a validation plan. I want to make sure our dedicated sizing gives you predictable SLAs once you go live.

Summary of Helix requirements (from our call):
- Streaming-first use case: token-by-token streaming for assistant responses, with visible first token within 150–200ms in most cases.
- Concurrency profile: 40–60 simultaneous active sessions during peak, average request size ~600 tokens, tail distributions produce 2–3x longer completions occasionally.
- Throughput target: reserved baseline to support 55 concurrent streams with median completion time under 900ms for short prompts and p95 start-of-stream < 250ms.
- Cost sensitivity: prefer smaller cluster with autoscaling buffer vs over-provisioning A100s if H100s show enough latency benefits.

Proposed Redwood validation plan (short):
1) Microbench matrix: run steady-state streaming + burst tests at concurrency levels {10, 25, 40, 55, 75} with 3 prompt-length tiers (short: 64 tokens, medium: 600 tokens, long: 2,048 tokens).
2) Hardware comparisons: H100 (4x), A100 (8x), and Ampere-class 3090/4080-style reference for cost baseline. We’ll capture first-token latency (streaming head), median completion time, p95 tail, and GPU utilization.
3) Batching/kv-cache scenarios: evaluate with and without prefix caching for repeated session patterns, and with batching windows tuned to meet first-token SLOs.
4) Acceptance criteria: p95 first-token <= 250ms, median end-to-end for medium prompts <= 900ms at 55 concurrency, GPU util < 80% steady-state to allow burst headroom.

Deliverables and timing:
- By July 17: validation matrix + schedule (spreadsheet) for your sign-off.
- By July 24: baseline bench results (pdf) for H100 vs A100 vs reference card, and recommended Reserved Throughput (RPS and concurrency) per cluster.

Next actions for Alex / HelixAI:
- Confirm the 55 concurrent streams baseline and share any representative prompt sets or preference for batching sensitivity (e.g., strict real-time vs allowed 50–100ms batching).
- Approve Redwood to run microbench tests against a short sample of your API keys (we’ll use testing keys and isolated capacity).

I’ve attached a validation matrix skeleton to this message; Grace will follow up with scheduling for the runs.

Thanks —
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0187

From: Alex Chen <alex@helixai.com>

Cc: HelixAI Solutions Team <solutions@helixai.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity validation: latency / concurrency / streaming clarification

Rishi —

Thanks for the clear recap. This captures our needs well. A few clarifications from our side before you kick off tests: 

1) First-token latency: our UX team considers <200ms ideal for the first visible token; <250ms is acceptable if it materially lowers infra cost. Can you include both numbers in the report?
2) Concurrency profile: 55 is our expected steady peak but we do see short bursts to ~90 for 20–40s during launches. Can you include a short burst test to 90?
3) Prompts: I uploaded a small set of representative prompts to the shared Drive link you sent in the demo. Those include a mix of multi-turn context where prefix caching matters.

We are happy to provide a demo key for testing — I’ll DM you the key and ephemeral creds. Also, we want your recommendation on whether H100 buys enough latency headroom to reduce cluster size vs using A100s with more nodes.

Thanks —
Alex
Alex Chen
Head of Platform, HelixAI
alex@helixai.com
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@helixai.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2026 11:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity validation: latency / concurrency / streaming clarification

Alex —

Appreciate the prompt reply and the sample prompts. We’ll include both first-token <200ms and <250ms columns in the report so you can see trade-offs. A couple of logistical notes and the test cadence: 

- Burst test: we’ll run two burst shapes — step (sustained 90 concurrent for 30s) and ramp (40 -> 90 over 60s) — to observe autoscaling behavior and cold-start effects.
- Hardware matrix: we will test 3 representative instance profiles: H100 (single-slot 80GB), A100 (40GB), and an RTX-derived reference (GA102 style) to show relative cost-per-throughput.
- Batching policy: default batch-window = 20ms; we’ll test 0ms (no batching), 20ms, and 50ms to measure first-token impact.
- Caching: run a 50% cache-hit workload to reflect your multi-turn traffic.

Attached is the populated validation matrix (first pass) and a short PDF with our prior low-latency comparisons for similar workloads. We will anonymize any customer data and use your demo key for isolated runs.

Proposed schedule: 
- July 17 (EOD): you confirm demo key access + any special prompts to exclude.
- July 19–21: run hardware + burst tests (we’ll rotate instances to maintain comparable GPU hours).
- July 24: deliver benchmark pdf + recommended reserved throughput and a cost/latency trade-off sheet.

If that timeline works, I’ll lock the runs and share the results board link.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com
